# Functionality matrix

What libSACM implements, requirement by requirement. The canonical source is [`functionality-matrix.toml`](functionality-matrix.toml); the row format, status vocabulary and gate rules are described in [README.md](README.md). `SACM23-*` rows are obligations of the OMG SACM 2.3 standard; `LIB-*` rows are library capabilities and quality commitments.

| SACM23-XMI-001 | **Interchange roots.** `xmi::read` returns `Ok(ReadOutput)` with a `Document` (and its diagnostics, sorted per ADR 0011: SACM-XMI-010 for `xsi:type` and SACM-XMI-011 for `xmi:version` (LIB-COMPAT-001), and the Infos SACM-XMI-004 for a missing `xmi:id` and SACM-ID-004 for a padded one (SACM23-XMI-020, SACM23-XMI-025)) when every interchange root is an `AssuranceCasePackage` or `ArgumentPackage` element in the pinned SACM namespace `http://www.omg.org/spec/SACM/20220301` (D-NS-PIN). A root is the document element, or each element child outside the XMI namespace of an `XMI` element in the XMI 2.5.1 namespace `http://www.omg.org/spec/XMI/20131001`. Elements and attributes are matched by namespace URI and local name, never by prefix (any-prefix equivalence is SACM23-XMI-002). Each root becomes a parentless element of its kind, in document order, whose id is its `xmi:id`'s `xsd:ID` value (SACM23-XMI-025), or a generated id when it has none (SACM23-XMI-020). Its name is missing (ADR 0013) unless it has a `name` child, which SACM23-XMI-012 reads. A read root may carry only namespace declarations, `xmi:id`, `xmi:version` (reported as SACM-XMI-011 and otherwise ignored: XMI 2.5.1 identifies its version by namespace) and an `xmi:type` or `xsi:type` naming its own class; its content may be only white space, comments, processing instructions, one `name` child under SACM23-XMI-012's rules, and the children SACM23-XMI-016 reads. The wrapper may carry only namespace declarations and `xmi:version`. An empty root id is `ReadError::InvalidId` and a root id that repeats an earlier element's is `ReadError::DuplicateId` (SACM23-VAL-020, SACM23-VAL-001). Anything else is refused as `ReadError::Unsupported` at its location, never dropped (LIB-API-009): any other child element or attribute of a root, non-white-space text, an `id` attribute in no namespace or another namespace (at its name), the other ten package kinds as roots (SACM23-ART-001, SACM23-TERM-001, AC-002/003, ARG-014/015), a package-kind name in another namespace or none (LIB-COMPAT-004), an `XMI` element in another namespace (LIB-COMPAT-002), and an XMI-namespace element as a root or wrapper child (SACM23-XMI-019). A root or wrapper child whose local name is none of the twelve package-kind names, and a wrapper with no root, are refused with a `ReadError` whose `code()` is SACM-XMI-001, at that element; among the refusals found while reading the roots this takes precedence over `Unsupported`, so which roots get SACM-XMI-001 does not depend on what a release can read (an `XMI` element outside the XMI namespace is `Unsupported` before its children are classified, ADR 0016 D1). No document is returned beside a refusal (ADR 0015). | SACM23-XMI-002 | **Namespace-prefix independence.** `xmi::read` matches element and attribute names by expanded name (namespace URI and local name), and resolves the QName value of `xmi:type`/`xsi:type` against the namespaces in scope on the element that carries it, so the choice of prefix never changes the result. A document that SACM23-XMI-001 reads gives the same `ReadOutput`, with diagnostics equal apart from their locations, or the same refusal kind, code and location, whatever prefixes it uses for the SACM, XMI and XSI namespaces. This holds for a default namespace, for declarations on the wrapper or on the root, and for a prefix rebound on an inner element. A prefix confers nothing by its spelling: `xmi`, `xsi` or `sacm` bound to another URI is that other namespace. Namespace URIs compare as exact strings. `xmlns=""` means no namespace, and a refusal says so. Before it is resolved, a type value is collapsed by the XSD white-space rules. An undeclared prefix in a type value, or an unprefixed value with no default namespace, is `Unsupported`, as in SACM23-XMI-001; this departs from C++ `xmi_reader.cpp:597-658` (ADR 0016 D2). | SACM23-XMI-011 | **String values survive XML exactly.** Every string value written as an XML attribute (today an element id and a name's `lang` and `content`) reads back exactly. `xmi::write` escapes `&`, `<`, `>` and `"`, and writes TAB, LF and CR as `&#9;`, `&#10;` and `&#13;`, so XML 1.0 §3.3.3 attribute normalisation cannot change them. A string holding a character outside XML 1.0 `Char` makes `xmi::write` fail with `UnrepresentableCharacter` naming the element and the character, and nothing is returned. For a LangString, an absent `lang` or `content` is written as no attribute and reads back absent; an empty one is written as `=""` and reads back empty (ADR 0012). The reader keeps every value exactly, with no trimming or normalisation beyond what XML 1.0 itself does. Every later LangString role inherits these rules. | LIB-RT-001 | **Semantic comparison.** `sacm::compare::semantic_compare(left, right) -> Vec<Difference>` compares two documents by their SACM content and lists every difference, naming the element id and the feature; an empty result means equal, and `Document: PartialEq + Eq` means exactly that (ADR 0020). Elements are matched by id. Compared: presence, kind, parent, name, the `xmi:id` of the name (`NameId`, SACM23-XMI-022), `assertionDeclaration`, the order of the roots and the relative order of each element's children across roles. Values are compared exactly: a missing name differs from every present name, including `<name/>` (`LangString::default()`) and `content=""`. Not compared: the generated-id counters, which are not SACM content. Formatting, attribute order and prefixes are not held by a `Document`. MultiLangString values are compared in order, though the metamodel does not order `value` (UtilityElement `content` and TaggedValue `key`, SACM23-BASE-004/005). The result is deterministic and in a fixed order, and comparison never panics.<br>_Note: Slice 0031: designed in ADR 0020. The generated-id counters are excluded so that LIB-RT-003 can hold; LIB-EDIT-002 checks the next generated id on its own. | SACM23-XMI-010 | **Read refusals are located at what they refuse.** Every `ReadError` from `xmi::read` carries the line and column of the construct it refuses: lines end as in XML 1.0 §2.11, columns count characters, and a leading byte order mark takes no column. An element is located at the `<` of its start tag, an attribute at the first character of its qualified name, text at its first character in the input that is not literal white space (a CDATA section or a character reference is located at its start), and a DOCTYPE at `<!DOCTYPE`. A well-formedness error is located where the input stops being well-formed, or at the end of a truncated input. An unsupported encoding is located at its name, or at line 1, column 1. Only a refusal for the parser's capacity limits has no location.<br>_Note: Moved to M1 by the maintainer, 2026-11-12: edited documents must reload, and M1's round-trip rows need it. | LIB-COMPAT-007 | **Strict save writes only valid models.** `WriteOptions` carries a save mode, strict by default (ADR 0022). Strict write runs `validation::validate` after the `NoRoot` check; if it reports any Error the write fails with `WriteError::Invalid`, which holds every Error diagnostic `validate` reported, in its order, and nothing is returned. Warnings and Infos never refuse. Tolerant write does not validate and writes the document as it is held, including a missing name. The writer's own checks follow and name the first failure (ADR 0017 W4). The refusal has no catalog code; its diagnostics carry theirs. Both modes write the same bytes for any document both write. A rule added in a later minor release can make a strict write that succeeded before refuse; that is documented and not a breaking change. Strict output is a document `validate` finds no Error in, and is schema-conforming once SACM23-VAL-020 checks ids read from files.<br>_Note: ADR review, 2026-11-13: decided in the load and save modes ADR with LIB-COMPAT-001: the semver stance (a new validation rule can make the default save fail in a minor release), and the reporting rule (every affected element, ADR 0013, or the first, ADR 0017 W4). Must land before any release (LIB-QA-005). Slice 0035: designed in ADR 0022, which takes over ADR 0013 amendment 1. | SACM23-XMI-014 | **Element form of single-valued values.** `xmi::read` reads, in both modes and with no diagnostic, the XML element form of the single-valued DataType properties it reads today: a `name`'s `lang` and `content`, and an Assertion's `assertionDeclaration` (in this release a Claim); `gid` (SACM23-BASE-006) and a `value`'s `lang` and `content` (SACM23-BASE-004) use it too, and later rows for `isCitation` and `isAbstract` inherit it. A value element is in no namespace, carries no attribute and has no element children; its value is its character content exactly (CDATA and references give their characters, comments and processing instructions are ignored, nothing is trimmed: XSD `preserve`), an empty element is the empty string, and an `assertionDeclaration` value must be one of the six literals exactly. The element may appear anywhere among its siblings, and the attribute and element forms may be mixed across different properties. The same document in either form reads to an equal `Document`, and export writes the attribute form. A property written both as an attribute and as an element, or as two elements, is refused in both modes as `ReadError::RepeatedValue` (SACM-MULT-001), naming every occurrence, even when the values are equal (the maintainer, 2026-11-13). A value element with an attribute (`xmi:id`, a type, `xsi:nil`, or the legacy `lang` on `content`), an element child, or a namespace stays `Unsupported` at the offending construct (LIB-COMPAT-003, LIB-COMPAT-008, SACM23-XMI-026); a bad literal is `ReadError::InvalidLiteral` at the start tag (SACM23-VAL-006).<br>_Note: Slice 0039: reworded for SACM23-XMI-020/-021/-022/-025 and SACM23-VAL-006 (ADR 0024, ADR 0021 amendment 2); re-check there. | LIB-API-008 | **Containment legality.** The model knows, for every (parent kind, child kind) pair, whether a SACM 2.3 composite role of the parent's class admits the child, per ptc/22-03-13 with the inventory's recorded divergences. The roles are ModelElement `description`, `implementationConstraint`, `note` and `taggedValue`; AssuranceCasePackage `assuranceCasePackage`, `argumentPackage`, `artifactPackage` and `terminologyPackage`; ArgumentPackage `argumentElement`; TerminologyPackage `terminologyElement`; ArtifactPackage `artifactElement`; and ArtifactAsset `property`. Subclasses inherit roles, package interfaces and bindings included. Every insertion refuses a child whose kind no role of the parent's class admits, and leaves the document unchanged; this binds the crate-internal insertion that the XMI reader and edit operations use, and the test-support `insert`. ArtifactPackage `artifactElement` admits every ArtifactElement kind, as the metamodel types it (ADR 0014). A root must be a package kind (`ElementKind::is_package`: the four packages, their interfaces and bindings; ADR 0010 D1 "of any package kind"); any other root is refused with `InsertError::RootNotAllowed`, as C++ refuses it (`io/xmi_reader.cpp` read_root, `is_package_kind`, `kXmiInvalidRoot`). Multiplicity is not enforced on insertion (D-VAL-LAYER, D-DESC-MULT). | SACM23-XMI-016 | **Containment children conform to their role.** `xmi::read` reads each containment child under its role element: an element in no namespace whose local name is a composite role of the parent's class, as spelled in ptc/22-03-13. The child's class is the one its `xmi:type` or `xsi:type` names, resolved as for roots (SACM23-XMI-002); without a type attribute it is the role's declared type, if that type is concrete (XMI 2.5.1 §7.6.3). The child is read with its `xmi:id`, its name (SACM23-XMI-012) and its parent, in document order across roles (ADR 0010 D2). In this release the readable children are an AssuranceCasePackage in `assuranceCasePackage`, an ArgumentPackage in `argumentPackage` and in `argumentElement`, and a Claim in `argumentElement`; each may carry only namespace declarations, `xmi:id`, a type attribute, one `name`, one `gid` (SACM23-BASE-006), utility children (SACM23-BASE-004/005) and, on a Claim, one `assertionDeclaration` as an attribute or an element (SACM23-XMI-017, SACM23-XMI-014). A child is never re-roled, re-typed or dropped: a type that does not conform to the role, a type naming an abstract or unknown class, a missing type under an abstract role, a role the parent's class lacks, a namespace-qualified role element, and any other child or attribute are refused as `ReadError::Unsupported` at the child's start tag, or at an attribute's name (ADR 0015's interim rule, as ADR 0016 D6 does for roots). `xmi::write` writes each child under the one role that admits it, for all 339 legal pairs, and what it writes for any document `edit::apply` builds reads back to the same ids, kinds, names, parents and order.<br>_Note: Slice 0025: owns strict import requiring the type attribute on an abstract-role child (SACM-XMI-005), moved from SACM23-XMI-006. Export writes `xmi:type` (ADR 0017); import accepts `xmi:type` and `xsi:type`. Moved to M1 by the maintainer, 2026-11-12: edited documents must reload, and M1's round-trip rows need it. Slice 0029 (lead decisions, the minimal options): only kinds whose model row is verified are read (ADR 0016 D5); non-conforming children are `Unsupported`, not coded (ADR 0015's interim rule, as ADR 0016 D6 does for roots); `assertionDeclaration` stays with SACM23-XMI-017; namespace-qualified role elements are refused, as for `name`. Moved out: references (SACM23-XMI-005 and the kind rows); utility children (SACM23-BASE-004/005); `gid`, `isCitation`, `isAbstract` (SACM23-BASE-006/007/008); strict SACM-XMI-003 and tolerant preservation (LIB-COMPAT-003); SACM-XMI-005 (LIB-COMPAT-010); a missing id (SACM23-XMI-020); a duplicate id (SACM23-VAL-001); `argumentationElement` (SACM23-XMI-009); element forms (SACM23-XMI-014/015); XMI metadata (SACM23-XMI-019); legacy shapes (LIB-COMPAT-008). C++ difference: C++ matches role elements by local name in any namespace (`xmi_reader.cpp:1988`); this crate refuses a namespace-qualified role element. Basis: role elements are local declarations, the XMI schema's default is unqualified, and XMI 2.5.1 rule 2a says "The namespace prefix is ignored for an object that is the value of a Property", which is ambiguous; the refusal is reversible and closes with LIB-COMPAT-003 (tolerant) if real files need it. Slice 0030: `assertionDeclaration` on a Claim is read (SACM23-XMI-017), so the attribute refusal narrows to non-Assertion children; re-checked there. | SACM23-XMI-017 | **assertionDeclaration in XMI.** `xmi::read` reads the `assertionDeclaration` XML attribute, in no namespace, on every readable Assertion kind: in this release a Claim (SACM23-XMI-016), and each later Assertion kind's read row inherits this rule. After XML 1.0 attribute-value normalisation, with no trimming or case folding, the value must be exactly one of `asserted`, `needsSupport`, `assumed`, `axiomatic`, `defeated` or `asCited`, and it reads as that literal. An absent attribute reads as `asserted`; an explicit `assertionDeclaration="asserted"` is accepted without a diagnostic and reads equal to the absent form. Any other value (another letter case, white space anywhere, the empty string, another word) is `ReadError::InvalidLiteral` (SACM-ENUM-001, SACM23-VAL-006) at the attribute's name, holding the value as read, and is never mapped to `asserted`. The attribute stays `Unsupported` on a non-Assertion element and when namespace-qualified; the element form is read by SACM23-XMI-014. `xmi::write` writes no attribute for `asserted` and otherwise `assertionDeclaration` with the exact literal, after `xmi:id`, on every element of an Assertion kind (all six) and on no other. Every literal round-trips on a Claim.<br>_Note: Slice 0030: moved from M2 to M1, because the reader refused most real files at their first Claim (the maintainer, 2026-11-13). C++ differences: C++ maps an unknown literal to `asserted` with SACM-ENUM-001, losing the raw value, and `justification` to `axiomatic` with a TaggedValue (`xmi_reader.cpp:1766-1794`); this crate refuses both until SACM23-VAL-006 and LIB-COMPAT. C++ matches the attribute in any namespace; this crate refuses `sacm:assertionDeclaration`. Editorial defect: §11.11 writes `assertionDeclared` for `assertionDeclaration`. Slice 0037: the element form of `lang` and `content` (and of `assertionDeclaration`) is read now (SACM23-XMI-014); reworded and re-checked there. | LIB-API-009 | **The reader refuses what it cannot represent.** `xmi::read` never returns a document that is missing content from its input (D-PRESERVE). Well-formed input that it cannot fully represent is refused with `ReadError::Unsupported`, which has no catalog code and carries a reason and a location: content that no verified row reads yet (SACM23-XMI-001 reads the first package roots), UTF-16 without a byte order mark, UTF-32 or UCS-4 input, and a declared encoding other than UTF-8 or ASCII in input without a UTF-16 byte order mark (SACM23-XMI-018 reads UTF-16 with one). A declared UTF-8 or ASCII encoding is accepted in any letter case; a byte of 0x80 or above under an ASCII declaration is malformed (SACM-XML-001). | SACM23-XMI-018 | **UTF-16 input.** `xmi::read` reads UTF-16 input that begins with a byte order mark (`FF FE` little-endian, `FE FF` big-endian, not followed by `00 00`). It decodes the input with std only (`u16::from_le_bytes`/`from_be_bytes`, `char::decode_utf16`) and then reads it exactly as the same characters in UTF-8, so the `ReadOutput` or `ReadError` is the same. Locations count characters as for UTF-8, and the byte order mark takes no column. The encoding declaration may be absent or name `UTF-16`, `UTF-16LE` or `UTF-16BE`, in any letter case. Any other declared name contradicts the mark and is `Malformed` (SACM-XML-001, XML 1.0 §4.3.3). So are an odd byte count and an unpaired surrogate. Everything else stays `Unsupported`, as in LIB-API-009: UTF-16 without a byte order mark (nothing is guessed), UTF-32 and UCS-4, and a UTF-16 name declared in UTF-8 input. A test reads the suite's 21 catalogs and runs through `xmi::read` every TEST with TYPE `not-wf`, RECOMMENDATION XML1.0 (the default), XML1.0-errata2e/3e/4e, NS1.0 or NS1.0-errata1e, VERSION absent or listing 1.0, and EDITION absent or listing 5. Each is refused: `Malformed` or `Doctype`, or `Unsupported` only from the encoding steps; a root-stage result (`Ok`, `InvalidRoot`, `NoPackage`, root-stage `Unsupported`) counts as accepted, because the suite's documents are not SACM. The one case roxmltree 0.21.2 accepts, rmt-ns10-032 (`xmlns:xmlns` declared), is refused by a new check (Namespaces 1.0 §3), so the list of accepted cases is empty and the parser's leniencies within the suite form a closed, reviewed list. Valid and invalid XML 1.0 and NS 1.0 cases that reach the root stage are never refused as `Malformed` (a guard against an over-strict scan). | SACM23-VAL-010 | **MultiLangString language uniqueness.** `validation::validate` reports, for every MultiLangString a document holds (each present UtilityElement `content` and TaggedValue `key`), one SACM-MULT-001 Error when it has no values (§8.5 `[1..*]`), and one SACM-MULT-001 Error for each language held by two or more of its values (§8.5 "must be unique"). `lang` is compared exactly (ADR 0012): two absent are equal; absent, `""` and `en` differ; `en`/`EN` and `en`/`en ` differ. It also reports a TaggedValue with no `key` as SACM-MULT-001 (§8.12 `key:MultiLangString[1]`; ptc `[1..1]`; D-SEV).
